# SR3H: services, expertise and research

Canonical website: https://sr3h.uk/
Organization: SR3H LTD
Company number: 17281224
Location: Oxford, United Kingdom
Contact: hello@sr3h.uk

## What SR3H does

SR3H is an independent technology lab in Oxford. It studies how AI is changing the relationship between people, the web and information, and builds useful software and dependable human-AI systems. Its work includes human-AI interaction, AI-mediated discovery, answer engine optimisation (AEO), AI agents and MCP, as well as context, knowledge, permissions, evidence and evaluation.

## AI, the web and emerging interaction

People increasingly describe what they need in a conversation rather than searching only with short keywords. AI systems can interpret intent, gather information from different sources, compare options and help people take action. SR3H studies this path from a person's question to the answer or choice they receive.

Research areas include conversational and agentic search, AI-mediated product and service discovery, AEO and generative engine optimisation (GEO), human-AI interaction, agent tools and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We ask what evidence informs an answer or recommendation, why suitable options may be missed, and how people can distinguish useful information from sponsored or otherwise commercially influenced results. These are questions we investigate, not claims that visibility alone produces a good recommendation or business outcome.

## AI visibility and discoverability

SR3H helps UK businesses understand and improve how AI systems find, describe and consider them for relevant customer needs. This work covers AI visibility, AI discoverability, AI search optimisation, answer engine optimisation (AEO), generative engine optimisation (GEO), large language model optimisation (LLMO), entity understanding, structured data, crawler access, retrieval, citations, representation quality, referral traffic and conversion measurement. The wider research asks whether an option is appropriate to the need, what evidence supports its selection, and how organic and sponsored visibility are presented.

An SR3H assessment can examine public crawlability, robots directives, sitemaps, canonical identity, structured data, service clarity, public evidence, answer consistency and the boundary between being technically discoverable and being commercially selected.

A technical check cannot by itself prove that an AI system will rank, cite or recommend a company. It also cannot prove customer demand, causal improvement or conversion performance. Those conclusions require controlled observations and real outcome data.

## Signal by Sr3h

Signal is one SR3H research programme. It combines a public website check with evidence-led research into AI-mediated commercial discovery. It distinguishes observed evidence from inference, keeps consumer and API observations separate, and separates natural discovery from introduced evaluation. Its purpose is to understand how AI systems represent choices and whether tested changes lead to better decisions and real-world outcomes.

Public page, website check and workspace access: https://sr3h.uk/signal.html

## Market Loop

Market Loop helps businesses understand how AI finds and recommends them, improve how they are represented, and learn from which customers actually convert. It connects public representation work with measured commercial outcomes rather than treating visibility as an end in itself.

## Signal Website Check

The website form tests whether search and AI systems can access and understand a business website. When its live discovery layer is available, it also runs a small dated sample of one branded and five business-specific unbranded searches using SR3H's bounded API service. The separate MCP inspects the website and can prepare and summarise a ten-question check without calling the OpenAI API; compatible ChatGPT sessions perform any optional research with their own available tools. Results use exact observed counts, not a score. They do not establish a fixed ranking, future recommendation, demand or conversion performance.

MCP endpoint: https://mcp.sr3h.uk/mcp
Support: https://sr3h.uk/ai-presence-support.html

## Conchup

Conchup is a workspace for complex software projects. It keeps requirements, decisions, implementation, tests and evidence connected, so a product can change without losing why it was built that way.

Public overview: https://sr3h.uk/conchup.html

## Blog

SR3H publishes a blog on AI, software engineering, product research and the systems it is building at https://sr3h.uk/journal.html.

Published posts include “Everyone wants a better answer. Better for whom?” on customer fit and business visibility; “Big Brain AI Monster” on the processes behind an AI answer; “Is AI visibility optimisation just SEO dressed up?” on the evidence for AI visibility work; “When buyers ask AI, who gets the work?” on AI discoverability; “Who owns the context?” on Brane, local AI and user-controlled context; and “The road we meant to take” on Good Route, route choice and navigation that respects a rider's intent.
